text: The Government Medical College, Srinagar (also known as GMC Srinagar) is a government medical college and hospital situated in Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir, India. It was established in 1959 and is the oldest medical college in Kashmir. The institution is affiliated with the University of Kashmir and recognised by the Medical Council of India (currently National Medical Commission). Located in the Karan Nagar area of Srinagar, it is approximately 1.5 km (0.93 mi) from Lal Chowk. The girls' hostel is on campus, while the boys' hostel is one km (0.62 mi) away. The college features well-equipped laboratories. Admission is based on merit through the National Eligibility and Entrance Test. In the 1950s, the government of Jammu and Kashmir identified the need for a medical college in the region. On 13 June 1957, then Prime Minister of India, Jawaharlal Nehru, laid the foundation stone. The college was initially named Jammu and Kashmir Medical College and began operations in 1959 with its first batch of students. It was initially located at the Shri Maharaja Hari Singh Hospital in Srinagar. In 1962, it was relocated to its current site in Karan Nagar, covering an area of around 100 acres. In 1970, it was renamed Government Medical College Srinagar and was affiliated with the University of Kashmir that year. In 1982, the first postgraduate batch was admitted. In 1998, it received recognition from the Medical Council of India (MCI) for both undergraduate and postgraduate medical programs. The college has several academic blocks housing classrooms, laboratories, and libraries. It also has an auditorium that can accommodate about 500 people, used for academic and cultural events. Sports facilities include a playground and outdoor sports such as basketball, as well as cricket and football grounds located in the boys' hostel campus. Currently, the college has eight associated hospitals. Its geographical coordinates are 35°07′57″N 74°50′15″E (35.1326°N 74.8375°E).
